title: How does a small classifier choose an answer?
description: Synthetic learning material illustrating the format, not a real paper or experiment result.
goal: Explain how inputs, scores and a selection rule produce a prediction.
view_reason: Explore how scores and a selection rule jointly contribute to a prediction.

concepts.title: Input numbers
concepts.summary: Start with the material the model receives.
body: This synthetic example uses two numbers as input. Choosing an input and choosing an answer are different tasks.
concepts.example: Consider the illustrative input [2, 5]. These numbers do not represent a real image or person.

concepts.title: A score for each answer
concepts.summary: Process the input to score each candidate.
body: The synthetic model produces a score for each answer. These scores are neither probabilities nor measured performance.
concepts.example: For illustration, let the score for A be 1.2 and the score for B be 2.4.

concepts.title: The selection rule
concepts.summary: Decide how to compare the scores.
body: This synthetic example selects the highest score. A different rule could produce a different answer from the same scores.
concepts.example: With a highest-score rule, choose 2.4 over 1.2.

concepts.title: The final prediction
concepts.summary: Use the scores and selection rule together to choose an answer.
body: Scores alone do not determine the prediction. A rule for interpreting them is also required.
Select a concept in the outline or follow the relationships below. Reading does not record understanding.
concepts.example: With illustrative scores A=1.2 and B=2.4 and a highest-score rule, the answer is B.
